To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the position of the centroid of the cluster, measured with a laser, was found to be independent of the irradiation profile.
we have measured the position dependence of the charge collection properties in the inhomogeneously exposed detector.
we have measured the position dependent charge collection in a prototype silicon microstrip irradiated to a peak fluence of 4.6 × 10 14 p/cm 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterisation of an in- homogeneously irradiated silicon microstrip detector.
the development of silicon microstrip detectors for the ATLAS experiment at LHC, with particular emphasis on the effects induced by non-uniform irradiations.
the study of the effects of inhomogeneous irradiations on the performance of silicon strip detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of inhomogeneous irradiations, at least in the case of the prototype detector studied here, are small enough to be neglected for the purpose of LHC tracking.
no evidence was found for any position dependent charge collection inhomogeneities.
the effects of non-uniform irradiations on the spatial resolution of a microstrip detector can be considered as negligible for the LHC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distortions due to non-ununiform irradiation can be kept within 10% for the LHC inner tracker region.
, within the limits of our experimental precision, the non-uniform irradiated microstrip sensor behaves in a similar way to the uniform one.
the effects due to non-ununiform irradiation are not significant for the LHC environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inhomogeneous irradiations of the type studied here do not appear to introduce significant distortions in the charge collection properties.
the spatial resolution of a microstrip detector can be maintained in the presence of large gradients in the fluence.
the distortions due to non-ununiform irradiation are small and can be neglected.
